passage: Every time Rukmini spoke in the marketing meeting, Aparna looked at the ceiling. In the pantry she turned her back. Nobody at the firm could say why. Rukmini spent a week bringing her tea, offering to share notes, laughing a bit too hard at Aparna's jokes. Nothing changed. On Friday evening, walking to the metro, she asked herself just once: had she ever taken credit that was Aparna's, or spoken sharply? She went through the months slowly and found nothing. It stung. But she made herself stop. Monday she said a normal good morning, and when Aparna did not answer, she simply went to her desk. She did not complain to anyone or hint at anything. Her lunch with two other colleagues was easier than it had been in weeks.

qa.q: What did Aparna do whenever Rukmini spoke in the meeting?
Why did Rukmini keep offering tea and notes for a week?
qa.a: She wanted Aparna's approval and hoped kindness would end the dislike. It hurt when nothing changed.

qa.q: What could Rukmini do if Aparna's coldness continues?
qa.a: She can keep being polite and professional, keep her good relationships with others, and speak to a supervisor only if it starts affecting her work.

qa.q: How might Aparna see Rukmini's changed behaviour on Monday?
qa.a: Aparna may notice that Rukmini has stopped trying so hard and simply says good morning. The passage does not say what Aparna thinks or why she dislikes her.

grounding: A peer openly dislikes the protagonist for no clear reason; she reflects once, then stops chasing approval without retaliating.

passage: From the first week of the architecture course in Copenhagen, Emil made it clear he didn't like Mina. He rolled his eyes when she spoke in studio, moved his desk when she sat nearby and once said loudly, 'Here comes the favourite.' Mina went over it at night. Had she interrupted him? Taken his spot? She asked her flatmate Sofie, who had been in most of those classes. 'Honestly? You haven't done anything,' Sofie said. So on Monday Mina tried once, directly: 'Emil, if I've upset you, I'd like to know.' He shrugged. 'You haven't. You're just not my type of person.' Mina felt the old urge to win him over, to bring cake, to be extra nice. She didn't. She moved her model to the window table and spent the afternoon on her roof design.

qa.q: What did Emil once say loudly?
What was Mina feeling after Emil shrugged?
qa.a: Mina felt hurt and a pull to win Emil over, but also some relief in deciding not to chase him.

qa.q: What went right in how Mina handled it?
qa.a: Mina checked once with Sofie and once with Emil whether she had done wrong, then stopped chasing approval and returned to her work.

qa.q: How does Emil seem to see Mina?
qa.a: Emil treats Mina as 'the favourite' and not his type, a dislike he cannot point to any real reason for.

grounding: Shows someone disliked for no clear reason who checks once whether she did wrong, then stops chasing approval.

passage: At the customer-service training centre in Noida, the trainer read out pairs for the mock-call exercise. When she read 'Kiran and Neelam', Kiran said, not quietly, 'Anyone but her, ma'am.' The room laughed nervously. Neelam's face burned. She had barely spoken to Kiran in three weeks. In the tea break she ran through everything: the seat she had taken on day one, a joke she had made about accents. She went up to Kiran by the water cooler. 'Did I say something that hurt you?' 'No,' Kiran said, not looking up. 'I just don't like you.' Back at her desk, Neelam typed a sharp message about Kiran for the batch group, then deleted it. She did the mock call with Kiran anyway, calmly. That night she told her cousin the whole story and felt lighter by the end.

qa.q: What did Kiran say when the pairs were read out?
What was Neelam feeling when the room laughed?
qa.a: Neelam felt embarrassed and hurt, her face burning, and began searching her memory for what she had done wrong.

qa.q: What would you advise Neelam if Kiran keeps this up?
qa.a: Keep doing what she did: stay calm, do the work, skip the sharp group message, and talk it through with people she trusts.

qa.q: How does Kiran seem to see Neelam?
qa.a: Kiran openly dislikes Neelam without any reason Kiran can name, and is willing to show it in front of everyone.

grounding: Shows a trainee openly disliked by a peer, who asks once whether she caused it, resists retaliating and stops chasing approval.
